title: 50 Years of "The Night of the Pencils" Spark Debate in La Plata

subtitle: Commemoration of Two Decades of Repression's End Sparks Student and Political Mobilizations

author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The remembrance of the 50th anniversary of "The Night of the Pencils" in La Plata has reignited debates about memory and justice, prompting student mobilizations and tensions within Peronism. The event, marking half a century since the military's invasion of students in 1976, brought to light the regime's legacy of violence and the need to preserve the victims' memory.

Survivors' Memory Receives Academic Recognition

In 2024, the National University of La Plata awarded honoris causa degrees to three survivors of the operation – Emilse Moler, Gustavo Calotti, and Pablo Díaz – and to relatives of disappeared students. The recognition was part of an effort to reconstruct history and remember that six of the ten students are still missing.

Student Mobilization and Internal Peronist Conflict

During the September 16 march, the Federation of Secondary Students (FES) and the Democratic Front Movement (MDF) coordinated their participation, but disagreements arose when Axel Kicillof's government did not offer transportation for the students. FES demanded that each organization arrange its own transfer, while the government offered limited logistical support.

Presence of Authorities and Inclusive Discourse

Governor Kicillof attended the march, accompanied by Vice Governor Verónica Magario and other ministers. He honored Moler, Calotti, and Professor Estela de Carlotto, emphasizing that memory must be preserved and that education continues with the guarantee of student transportation passes.

Political and Cultural Developments

The march also saw the participation of Kirchnerist figures, such as Senator Eduardo "Wado" de Pedro and Deputy Lucía Cámpora. The presence of artists and the screening of films like Héctor Olivera's work helped contextualize the history for today's youth.

Persistent Challenges and the Search for Justice

Despite advancements, questions remain about the ultimate fate of the six disappeared students. The lack of information and the silence of potential witnesses continue to hinder the conclusion of investigations. The government of Misiones, for example, organized the Youth Festival of Memory and Rights, reinforcing the importance of involving young people in the preservation of democracy.

With information from EL PAÍS, Infobae, Revista Códigos.
